result.title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation
result.summary: Long-term memory supports agents across sessions. Repeated retrieval and write-back can let one historical claim occupy multiple retrieval positions and influence current answers without independent evidence. Existing work examines retrieval, updating, and question answering, leaving same-source record accumulation and post-correction persistence underexplored. Motivated by research in social cognition and memory psychology on repeated exposure, retrieval, and revision, we define \emph{Memory Echo} as the excess retrieval exposure gained by historical information from the same source without additional independent evidence, and introduce MEchoBench to evaluate its emergence, correction resistance, persistence, and effect on answers. To address this phenomenon, we introduce the Family--Provenance--Authority framework (FPA). Specifically, FPA selects one representative per source family, conditions the eligibility of old records for the answer context on verified corrections, and constrains final answers with authoritative evidence. In paired replay on 190 fixed questions across four memory frameworks, FPA raises accuracy from 0.825 to 0.920 with DeepSeek V4 Flash and from 0.782 to 0.916 with Kimi K2.6; mean Decision Contamination Effect falls from 0.106 to 0.030 and from 0.109 to 0.038, respectively. These results show that agent memory can preserve traceable history without allowing repeated historical information to govern current decisions. The code is available at https://github.com/OrcasSam/memory-echo-benchmark.

AI.brief_summary: 论文定义「Memory Echo」为同源历史信息在缺乏独立证据下获得的额外检索曝光，构建 MEchoBench 评估其产生、抗纠正与持续影响，并提出 Family–Provenance–Authority 框架，在四个记忆框架的 190 个固定问题上提升准确率并降低决策污染。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作研究智能体长时记忆中的同源信息放大，与 LVR 主线无直接关联；但其「无新证据仍可反复主导当前决策」的问题表述，可能与 latent 迭代中状态自我强化、视觉证据筛选与溯源约束形成类比，可供核查。
